summary.name: GraphCode
summary.one_liner: A macOS app for running coding-agent sessions as a graph of loops on a canvas, where each loop is a live terminal you can attach to and steer mid-run.
use_cases: Running coding agents unattended on repeat
Chaining a triage, fixer and reviewer agent pipeline
Scheduling recurring agent tasks on a cadence
Steering a running coding agent mid-task
summary.what_it_does: GraphCode connects agent loops (sessions that run on repeat) as nodes on a canvas, with edges for hand-off, message, or spawn between them. Each loop runs in a persistent terminal session that survives quitting the app or rebooting, and you can click a node to attach to its live terminal. Loops can be turn-based, goal-based (stopping when a shell check exits 0), time-based (a cadence in the prompt), or composite. Loops can message each other across repos, and a guard caps the number of passes and stops after repeated idle passes. A CLI and a background daemon share a local socket with the app.
notable: Graph of agent loops with live, attachable terminals per node
Bounded loops with pass limits and stall detection; metric measured by the orchestrator, not the agent
Sessions persist across app quit, daemon restart and reboot
Per-loop memory digest so relaunched sessions resume with lessons learned
caveats: License is FSL-1.1-MIT, listed as freeware on awesome-mac; pricing not stated on the page
